item.title: Computability of states and non-computability of traces
item.description: arXiv:2611.28337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study computable presentations of the state space and trace space of computably presented C*-algebras. We show that the state space has a computably compact presentation with respect to which the evaluation of states is a computable map. As an application of having computable states, we obtain a computable version of the GNS construction. We show that the trace space does not share these computational properties. Specifically, we give an example of a computable presentation of a simple AF algebra for which the trace space has no computably compact presentation with respect to which evaluation is computable. As a consequence, we demonstrate that the Elliott invariant of a computably presentable classifiable C*-algebra is not always presentable in a way that makes all key features of the invariant computable.
item.dc:creator: Christopher J. Eagle

item.title: Similarity preserving noncommutative maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.28428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note we study similarity preserving automorphisms of noncommutative (NC for short) balls. We show that every similarity preserving NC automorphism is, in fact, given by a similarity with an NC invertible function. As an application, we show that the group of automorphisms of the free semigroup algebra is generated by unitarily implemented and inner automorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Eli Shamovich

item.title: Invariant subspaces and nest algebras in left-right operator splitting
item.description: arXiv:2611.28903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The left--right (L-R) splitting method for boundary integral equations in rough-surface scattering writes the integral operator as the sum of its lower- and strictly upper- triangular parts. This note examines the operator algebra formed by the lower-triangular ($L$-type) parts.Their weak closure is a nest algebra; second-kind $L$-type operators with Hilbert--Schmidt kernels have $L$-type inverses; and Arveson's distance formula expresses the error of the best possible forward-only approximation in terms of the backward coupling across a single cut. Bounds and numerical results for the 2D double-layer kernel suggest that truncation is close to optimal, and that the worst-case input field is a predominantly left-going grazing wave rather than backscatter of a right-going incident field. For a hard surface the inverse $L$-operator is given, up to a second-order correction, by four times the $L$-operator of the mirror-image surface, and several open questions are posed.
item.dc:creator: Mark Spivack

item.title: A Finiteness Result for Commuting Squares and Quantitative Ocneanu Rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2611.29535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the spanning relative commutant condition (SRC) for nondegenerate commuting squares of matrix algebras. The condition requires that the second relative commutant span the next algebra in the lower row of the basic construction as a right module over the preceding algebra. We prove that if a sequence of SRC squares with fixed tracial inclusion data converges, then all but finitely many terms are isomorphic to the limit square. We also show that the standard commuting square of every finite-index inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors of depth two satisfies SRC. This gives a commuting-square proof of Ocneanu's finiteness theorem for standard invariants with a prescribed finite principal graph. We then obtain the explicit bound $B(D)=10^{7D^5}$ for the number of SRC squares up to isomorphism when the upper-right tracial algebra is prescribed and has dimension $D$. The same function bounds the number of standard invariants with a prescribed finite principal graph when $D$ is the number of closed walks of length $6\ell$ at the root, where $\ell$ is the least odd integer at least the diameter. We also characterize the Hadamard matrices whose spin model commuting squares satisfy SRC. These are precisely the matrices equivalent to character tables of finite abelian groups.
item.dc:creator: Shannon Hall, Remus Nicoara

item.title: The Kaplansky-Aupetit conjecture for C*-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.29761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We settle the Kaplansky--Aupetit conjecture when either algebra is a $C^*$-algebra. More precisely, if $A$ is a unital Banach algebra and $B$ is a unital $C^*$-algebra, or if $A$ is a unital $C^*$-algebra and $B$ is a unital semisimple Banach algebra, then every unital invertibility-preserving linear surjection $\phi: A\to B$ is a Jordan homomorphism. In fact, it suffices to assume that $\phi$ preserves the invertibility of products of two exponentials, or of individual exponentials when both algebras are $C^*$-algebras. Claude Opus 5.5 found the original proof when both $A$ and $B$ are $C^*$-algebras by adapting a resolvent estimate from a recent preprint of Colbrook and Stepaniants, while OpenAI's GPT-6.1 further generalized this to the case where only one algebra is a $C^*$-algebra.
item.dc:creator: Ilja Gogi\'{c}, Bojan Kuzma

item.title: Orthogonal lifting and amenability in ultrapowers
item.description: arXiv:2611.29924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor and let $\omega$ be a free ultrafilter on $\mathbb{N}$. We prove that any two orthogonal separable amenable von Neumann subalgebras in the ultrapower $\mathcal{M}^{\omega}$ admit orthogonal finite-dimensional lifts. In particular, two independent unitary operators in $\mathcal{M}^\omega$ admit independent finite-spectrum representatives. We also show that the orthogonal lifting can fail whenever one of the subalgebras is nonamenable and Connes-embeddable.
item.dc:creator: Minghui Ma, Wenming Wu, Yifeng Ye

item.title: On the extension of non-faithful and non-normal traces of von Neumann algebras to their affiliated operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.30036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\tau$ be a positive tracial functional on a finite von Neumann algebra ${\mathcal{M}}$, not necessarily normal. For a positive self-adjoint operator $A$ affiliated with ${\mathcal{M}}$ we define ${\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}}(A)=\lim_{h\downarrow0}\tau(A(\mathrm{I}+hA)^{-1})\in[0,\infty]$. We show that $\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}(A)=\sup_R\tau(\min(A,R \mathrm{I}))$. We prove that ${\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}}$ is additive on positive affiliated operators, by a form--resolvent comparison valid for arbitrary positive traces. As a consequence, $\tau$ has a positive linear extension to the span $\mathscr D_\tau$ of the positive affiliated operators of finite extended trace, and $\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}(T^*T)$ defines a pre-Hilbert structure for every positive trace. For every trace, $\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}(|S+T|)^{2/3}\le \tau_{\mathrm{Y}}(|S|)^{2/3}+\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}(|T|)^{2/3}$; hence the operators $T$ with $\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}(|T|)<\infty$ form a ${\mathcal{M}}$-bimodule $\mathscr L_Y^1$, on which the linear extension is defined and cyclic. It turns out that $\mathscr L_Y^1=\mathscr D_\tau$; $d(S,T)={\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}}(|S-T|)^{2/3}$ is a translation-invariant pseudometric on $\mathscr L^1_Y$ and is a metric iff $\tau$ is faithful. On the approximation side, a Chernoff family in ${\mathcal{M}}$ forces affiliation of its generator. Trace defects of Chernoff families need not converge to ${\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}}(A)$, even for faithful normal traces, while two-sided resolvent comparison suffices. For faithful normal traces, ${\tau_{\mathrm{Y}}}$ is the canonical extension and the associated space $\mathscr L_Y^p$ coincide with the classical $L^p({\mathcal{M}},\tau)$ as well as their norms ($1\leq p<\infty$).
item.dc:creator: Comlan Edmond Koudjinan

item.title: Square-zero preservers and tracial states on C*-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.30109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a $C^*$-algebra $A$ of dimension at least two has no tracial states if and only if, for every complex normed space $E$, each bounded symmetric bilinear map $V:A\times A\to E$ with $V(x,x)=0$ for every square-zero $x\in A$ factors through the Jordan product, that is, $V(x,y)=S((xy+yx)/2)$ for some bounded linear map $S:A\to E$ and all $x,y\in A$. The factor $S$ is unique and $\|S\|=\|V\|$. Moreover, applying this bilinear result, we show that $A$ has no tracial states if and only if every bounded square-zero-preserving linear surjection $\phi:A\to B$ onto a nonzero Banach algebra with a bounded approximate identity factors as $\phi=WJ$, where $J:A\to B$ is a bounded Jordan homomorphism and $W:B\to B$ is a bounded invertible linear centralizer. Likewise, $A$ has no tracial states if and only if every spectrally bounded linear surjection $\phi:A\to B$ onto a nonzero semisimple Banach algebra with a bounded approximate identity admits such a factorization. In both cases, the factors are unique and $J$ induces a bounded Jordan isomorphism $A/\ker\phi\to B$. In particular, when $\phi$ is unital, the factorization reduces to $\phi=J$, which settles Mathieu's square-zero conjecture for nonscalar domains and answers the related question on spectrally bounded surjections.
item.dc:creator: Ilja Gogi\'{c}, Bojan Kuzma

item.title: Morita equivalence classification for irrational noncommutative solenoids
item.description: arXiv:2611.30400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a prime integer $p$, we define a $p$-angle to be an element of the $p$-solenoid ${\mathcal S}_p$ or equivalently an element of $\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{Q}_p$ modulo $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$. Noncommutative $p$-solenoids, or equivalently $p$-rotation algebras, are $C^*$-algebras defined by a $p$-angle in the same way as non-commutative tori or usual rotation algebras are defined by an angle. We give a complete classification, in terms of their $p$-angles and in the irrational case, of these $C^*$-algebras up to strong Morita equivalence, but also the associated groupoids up to Morita equivalence; more precisely, we obtain the following classification result: two irrational $p$-angles define strong Morita equivalent noncommutative solenoids if and only if they define isomorphic dimension groups if and only if they are congruent modulo $GL_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/p])$ if and only if they define Morita equivalent groupoids. This generalises, with a different proof, the classification up to isomorphism, previously obtained by Latr\'emoli\`ere and Packer. We also give a geometrical construction of projective $C^*$-modules in terms of proper $G$-spaces which exhaust the dimension group up to a shift and implement all relevant Morita equivalences by groupoid equivalences.
item.dc:creator: Paulo Carrillo Rouse, Laurent Guillaume, Jean Renault

item.title: Two-Dimensional Local Smoothing in Noncommutative Spaces and Its Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.30520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove local smoothing for planar half-waves with coefficients in a semifinite tracial von Neumann algebra $M$. For $N\ge2$ and $P_N=\psi(|D|/N)$ with $\psi\in C_c^\infty((1/2,2))$, we obtain $\|e^{it|D|}P_N f\|_{L^4([1,2]\times\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}\le C_\psi\sqrt{\log(2+N)}\|f\|_{L^4(\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}$ uniformly in $M$ and its trace. Pairing the Dirichlet energies for $M$ and its opposite algebra cancels a determinant contribution that can have either sign. At $p=4$, summation over frequency annuli gives local smoothing for every Sobolev order $s>0$. Interpolating the annular estimates before summation gives spacetime $L^p$ bounds for $2\le p\le\infty$ and Sobolev orders $s>\sigma(p)=\max\{0,1/2-2/p\}$, as well as logarithmically weighted bounds at $s=\sigma(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$. The finite-$p$ bounds transfer to quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes, answering the question of Hong, Lai and Wang about the range $s>\sigma(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$ on generalized Moyal planes. For $1<p<\infty$ and complex $\alpha$ with $\operatorname{Re}\alpha>\max\{2/p-1,1/p-1/2,-1/p\}$, we prove maximal inequalities over all radii for generalized circular means on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes. For an action $\beta$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ on $M$ by normal trace-preserving $*$-automorphisms with norm-continuous $L^p$ orbits, the orbit mean $A_{t,\beta}^\alpha x$ converges bilaterally almost uniformly to $\pi x/\Gamma(1+\alpha)$ as $t\downarrow0$ for every $x\in L^p(M)$. We also obtain estimates for truncated cone multipliers on three-dimensional Euclidean and quantum Euclidean spaces, and full-radius row and column bounds for Stein's square function on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes.
item.dc:creator: Xudong Lai, Siyu Liu

item.title: Trace-class perturbations of Voiculescu's free semicircular families
item.description: arXiv:2611.30882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\{s_j\}_{j\in\Lambda}$ be the standard free semicircular family on the full Fock space $\mathcal H=\mathcal F(\ell^2(\Lambda))$, where $|\Lambda|\geqslant2$. For any family $\{K_j\}_{j\in\Lambda}$ of self-adjoint trace-class operators with $\gamma=\sum_{j\in\Lambda}\|K_j\|_1<\infty$, we prove that the type $\mathrm{II}_1$ summand $\mathcal P$ of the von Neumann algebra $W^*(\{s_j+K_j\colon j\in\Lambda\})$ is isomorphic to the free group factor $\mathcal L(\mathbb F_\Lambda)$. As an application, we show that the set of irreducible operators on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is not dense in the trace-class norm. For each fixed $\gamma>0$, the possible values of the Murray--von Neumann dimension $\dim_{\mathcal P}(z_{\mathcal P}\mathcal H)$ form the interval $[1,1+\gamma)$, where $z_{\mathcal P}$ is the identity of $\mathcal P$.
item.dc:creator: Minghui Ma, Rui Shi, Tianze Wang

item.title: $C^*(\mathbb{F}_2\times\mathbb{F}_2)$ fails the local lifting property
item.description: arXiv:2611.31147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the full group \(C^*\)-algebra \(C^*(\F_k\times\F_m)\) fails the local lifting property for all integers \(k,m\ge2\), and therefore disprove Ozawa's Strong Kirchberg Conjecture. Our proof is inspired by a construction of Ioana concerning Hilbert--Schmidt stability. We then strengthen this result by showing that \(C^*(\F_k\times\F_m)\) does not locally embed into \(C^*(\F_\infty)\). Consequently, the lifting property, the local lifting property, and local embeddability into \(C^*(\F_\infty)\) are not preserved under maximal tensor products.
item.dc:creator: Jean Roydor

item.title: Algebras Generated by Two Idempotent Matrices: Classification up to Isomorphism and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.28086v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper is a continuation of the earlier work by the author and Falguni Roy \cite{biswas2025comprehensive} on the algebra \(\operatorname{alg}(P,Q)\) generated by two idempotent matrices \(P,Q\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}\). A complete classification of these algebras up to algebra isomorphism is presented, without imposing any additional restrictions on the idempotents. As an application, group invertibility in \(\operatorname{alg}(P,Q)\) is employed to obtain an explicit solution to a particular system of linear equations.
item.dc:creator: Rounak Biswas

item.title: Leavitt path algebras, growth series, Thompson groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.28188v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider several problems related to the growth of Leavitt path algebras with respect to the natural length filtration. We define the generating function of the series of dimensions of the successive quotients of this filtration and show that it is a rational function with poles which are reciprocal of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix, a fact which is related to recent results by Bock, Gil Canto, Mart\'in Barquero, Mart\'in Gonz\'alez, Ruiz Campos and Sebandal on algebraic entropy of Leavitt path algebras. We also consider the filtration induced in the topological full group of the Renault-Deaconu groupoid of the defining graph and study the growth of the associated series. In the particular case of Thompson's group $V$, we find double exponential upper and lower bounds for this growth. We also prove related results for the group $F$ and for some submonoids.
item.dc:creator: Conchita Mart\'inez-P\'erez, Sof\'ia Sir\'on

item.title: Semiclassical Weyl laws and noncommutative geometry on open manifolds with conformally cusp metrics
item.description: arXiv:2611.29139v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish semiclassical Weyl laws on open Riemannian manifolds with conformally cusp metrics of finite volume. These metrics need not be complete, and even when complete they do not have bounded geometry. Moreover, the potentials are bounded, the discreteness of the spectrum being a consequence of the geometry rather than of a confining potential. Therefore, our results lie beyond the scope of recent semiclassical Weyl laws of Dai--Yan and Braverman. The semiclassical Weyl laws are established for fractional Schr\"odinger operators associated with Dirac operators, magnetic Laplacians, and Hodge Laplacians, under conditions of Moroianu and Gol\'enia--Moroianu which ensure that these operators have discrete spectra. We also obtain extensions of Connes' integration formula for the same operators. In addition, we deal with a class of conformally cusp metrics of infinite volume, in which case the semiclassical Weyl laws and the integration formulas only involve the values at infinity. The results are obtained by applying the abstract semiclassical Weyl laws and integration formulas for spectral triples established in a previous paper.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Ponge

item.title: Continuity of almost commutative manifolds for the spectral propinquity
item.description: arXiv:2603.19128v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the canonical metric spectral triples of a fixed compact connected spin manifold depend continuously, for the spectral propinquity, on the Riemannian metric endowed with the $C^1$ topology. This continuity extends to almost commutative spectral triples, allowing the Riemannian metric and the Dirac operator of a fixed finite dimensional factor to vary simultaneously. We also establish continuity for metric spectral triples arising from ergodic actions of compact connected Lie groups as the inner product on the Lie algebra varies. Our proofs use a common continuity criterion involving graph norms and commutator seminorms. As a consequence, eigenvalues in any compact interval whose endpoints avoid the limiting spectrum converge with multiplicity. These results relate classical variations of metric data to the geometry of metric spectral triples.
item.dc:creator: Frederic Latremoliere

item.title: Relative norm averaging property and selflessness of almost periodic actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.35644v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $D$ be a unital separable $C^*$-algebra with a faithful state $\sigma$ and $G$ be a discrete group. We introduce a property called relative norm averaging property (RNA) for almost periodic $\sigma$-preserving actions by $G$ on $(D,\sigma)$. We prove that if an almost periodic $\sigma$-preserving action $\alpha$ satisfies that $\overline{\alpha(G)} \subseteq \text{Aut}(D,\sigma)$ is connected and nontrivial, then $\alpha$ satisfies (RNA). As an application, we prove that if $G$ has property PHP of Ozawa and $\alpha:G\curvearrowright (D,\sigma)$ is an ergodic (i.e. $D^G=\mathbb{C}$) almost periodic $\sigma$-preserving action with $\overline{\alpha(G)}$ being connected, then $D\rtimes_r G$ is selfless. This includes certain paradoxical isometric actions of $\mathbb{F}_2$ on the sphere. In non-ergodic case, we prove that the relative norm averaging property implies that $D\rtimes_r G$ satisfies the $D^G$-valued selfless, if $G$ satisfies PHP.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Toyota

item.title: Invariants of subfactors associated to Petrescu's Hadamard matrices of order 7
item.description: arXiv:2611.25638v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Petrescu's sixth-root $7 \times 7$ Hadamard matrix defines an irreducible, hyperfinite subfactor $N \subset M$ with Jones index 7. It is built from the spin model commuting square obtained from the Hadamard matrix by iterating Jones' basic construction. We prove that the standard invariant of this subfactor is minimal, i.e. the higher relative commutants consists of Temperley-Lieb algebras. Thus, the principal graphs of the subfactor are the Coxeter-Dynkin graph A$_\infty$. This solves a long-standing open problem. The main new idea is a congruence for the profile of the Hadamard matrix that restricts the order of rotation on the lowest-weight spaces in Jones planar algebra description of the standard invariant. Together with a uniform trace bound, this gives bounded annular multiplicities on a subsequence, which forces the principal graph to have norm at most two. We also show that the same result holds for most Hadamard matrices in Petrescu's one-parameter family. Specifically, the associated subfactors have Temperley-Lieb standard invariant at every transcendental phase and at every algebraic phase with residue $\pm1$ at a prime above three. In each fixed degree the exceptional set is finite and consists of algebraic numbers. Our methods apply to several other families of Hadamard matrices of order $q >4$ as well, and we show that the associated subfactors have A$_\infty$ principal graphs. These include real Hadamard matrices of order $q\equiv4\pmod8$, Hadamard matrices over $\Q(i)$ of order $q\equiv2\pmod4$ and cube-root matrices of order $q$ with $3\mid q$ and $9\nmid q$. For order six Hadamard matrices, we obtain the same result at every transcendental phase in Di\c{t}\u{a}'s family through Haagerup's matrix and at every algebraically independent pair of phases in Karlsson's two-parameter family.
item.dc:creator: Dietmar Bisch, Remus Nicoara

item.title: Amenability of group actions on compact spaces and the associated Banach algebras
item.description: arXiv:2504.08357v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a topological group $G$, amenability can be characterized by the amenability of the convolution Banach algebra $L^1(G)$. Here a Banach algebra $A$ is called amenable if every bounded derivation from $A$ into any dual--type $A$--$A$--Banach bimodule is inner. We extend this classical result to the case of discrete group actions on compact Hausdorff spaces in our main theorem Theorem 5.2. By using a Banach algebra naturally associated with the action and adopting a suitably weakened notion of amenability for Banach algebras, we obtain an analogous characterization of amenable actions. As a lemma, we also proved a fixed--point property for amenable actions in Theorem 4.4 that strengthens the theorem of Dong and Wang (2015).
item.dc:creator: Hikaru Awazu

item.title: Strong convergence of uniformly random permutation representations of surface groups
item.description: arXiv:2504.08988v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus at least two. Consider the composition of a uniformly random element of $\mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma,S_n)$ with the $(n-1)$-dimensional irreducible representation of $S_n$. We prove the strong convergence in probability as $n\to\infty$ of this sequence of random representations to the regular representation of $\Gamma$. As a consequence, for any closed orientable hyperbolic surface $X$, with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$, a uniformly random degree-$n$ covering space of $X$ has near optimal relative spectral gap --- ignoring the eigenvalues that arise from the base surface $X$. To do so, we show that the polynomial method of proving strong convergence can be extended beyond rational settings. To meet the requirements of this extension we prove two new kinds of results. First, we show there are effective polynomial approximations of expected values of traces of elements of $\Gamma$ under random homomorphisms to $S_{n}$. Secondly, we estimate the growth rates of probabilities that a finitely supported random walk on $\Gamma$ is a proper power after a given number of steps.
item.dc:creator: Michael Magee, Doron Puder, Ramon van Handel

item.title: An elementary proof of rational injectivity in equivariant KK-theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.31174v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Antonini, Azzali and Skandalis proved that, for every countable discrete group $\Gamma$, the canonical map $E\Gamma\to\underline{E}\Gamma$ induces a split injection in equivariant $KK$-theory with real coefficients. In this paper, we give a more elementary proof of the corresponding rational injectivity result in ordinary equivariant $KK$-theory without using $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors.
item.dc:creator: Denghui Luo, Geng Tian

item.title: Sharp $L_p$-Regularity for Quantum Markov Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.21411v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the sharp universal constants in positive-input $L_p$-regularity for finite-dimensional quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful invariant state. For $1<p<\infty$, they are $p\sin(\pi/p)/(2(p-1))$ under KMS symmetry and $\frac{p}{2(p-1)}\tan(\frac{\pi}{2}\min\{1/p,1-1/p\})$ without a symmetry assumption, with the endpoint values at $p=1$ given by $\pi/2$ and $\pi/4$, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Lijun Wang
